utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, may I remind you that you took a declaration yesterday to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing else but the truth. You are still bound by that declaration today. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lazarevic. As you will recall, at the end of the day yesterday we were finishing up our discussion of the 2nd of May, 1995 in relation to a couple of documents. I want to ask you one or two more questions about the 2nd of May before we move on. As far as you can recall, did the media report on the events in Zagreb on the 2nd of May that same evening?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that the media reported earlier during the same day. All the media, especially the Croatian radio and the Croatian television reported on the event, and that was the major headline, the breaking news of the day. The press also reported on the event, depending of course on the time of day the newspapers came out. Of course also in the press it was the breaking news, covered both by text and photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Was it clear from that media coverage that there had been civilian casualties or civilians were affected by the attack?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By all means, you're right. As the first news reports came out, it was quite clear what had transpired. Radio and TV reporters and press journalists went to the hospitals, talked to those who were injured, with the physicians and eyewitnesses. Statements were given by fire-fighters, police officers. The news coverage went hand in hand with the events of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And let me turn your attention now to the following day, to the 3rd of May, 1995. Where were you around noon on that day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day I was in my office, just as I had been the day before. I normally work for the better part of the morning and the afternoon, although the day before I stayed in my office until midnight, or perhaps even later, because I was trying to produce, along with my colleagues, a summary report of the events on the 2nd of May. I then went back home, had some sleep, and went back into the office to continue collecting information. In response to your question about the 3rd of May, at the critical time I was also in my office at Djordjiceva Street when the same type of explosion was heard -- or explosions were heard. It was the same thing all over again. Once again, I did my best to organise my service in order to collect as much information as possible. That would be my answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you able to personally visit any of the sites of impacts on that day, the 3rd of May?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had had an official car on my -- at my disposal for several years by then. As soon as I realised what had happened on the 3rd of May, I got into my car and went to Mazuranica Square, Trg Marsala Tita square, I toured these sites and organised on-site investigations which were to take place on these most recent sites. The sites on the 3rd of May were to be found to the west compared to the sites that had been affected the day before. At that point I realised that a pyrotechnist got killed at Klaiceva hospital as one of the bombs he was trying to deactivate exploded. That was one of the reasons for me to go to that particular site as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll come to that incident a little bit later. Right now I would like to hand you another document, if I could with the assistance of the usher, please. And perhaps -- here I have them in B/C/S. If we could give a copy to the witness, actually, this copy to the witness is bound, and for the Defence and Mr. Martic, if he pleases. And four copies for the Court. Thank you. The ERN of this document is 0365-5342 to 5443. And perhaps when the court officer gets back to her seat I can repeat that so they can be brought up on e-court. If it's easier, the doc ID in e-court will be 0365-5342. Mr. Lazarevic, maybe as we're waiting for it to come up on the screen, if you could just have a look through this report to familiarise yourself with it again. Okay, there we go, it's our screens. In fact, Your Honours, for clarification, this first page in e-court is another document. I will have that removed afterwards. We released in time to take the first page off of the copies we gave to Your Honours and to the witness. So if on e-court we could actually go to the second page, please. That's the correct page. And the ERN for the beginning of report is 0365-5343. Mr. Lazarevic, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What is it, please?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the official record of the inspection of the scene, which I myself compiled, and has to do with the rocket attack on Zagreb on the 3rd of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you could look, I believe, at page 82 in B/C/S, it's page 78, Your Honours, in the English version. The ERN is 0365-5423, we can also see it on the screen. If we could scroll down a bit on the screen, please. Mr. Lazarevic, is that your signature that appears there on this report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm trying to follow you both on the screen and on paper, and it looks like I miss you on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: On the e-court I am getting it, Your Honour, the B/C/S version on the screen. It looks to be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're looking at the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now at least I've got a document that bears the witness's name. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, did you prepare this report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I produced the entire report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And did you compile the information for this report in essentially the same way that you compiled the information for the report you described -- we looked at, in fact, yesterday covering the 2nd of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I compiled this official record on the inspection of the scene of the incident in exactly the same way. Because on the first page I listed the persons, my colleagues who were involved in the on-site investigation process. All of us enumerated here took part in the on-site investigation. Every single person wrote his or her own report, which I then included in this official record.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. As with the report we looked at yesterday, I'm going to try to go through it fairly quickly, although it contains a lot of information. My first question is: What locations are dealt with in this report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report dated the 3rd of May, 1995, covers an area which is somewhat to the west compared to the sites affected the day before, as I said before. Therefore, the locations include Mrazoviceva Square, Trg Marsala Tita square, where the Croatian National Theatre can be found, the Klaiceva children's hospital, and the old people's home that can be found directly to -- on this street. Furthermore, on the 3rd of May one rocket landed at Novi Zagreb in the Cehi neighbourhood, but according to the information I had, the rocket was not activated or didn't open up, but we located the site of its impact, or rather the site where it landed, so it is included in the report. It is furthermore described in the sketches, and it can be found in the photographs, all of which form a component part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And were there also impacts at one location to the east of the centre of Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. How shall I put it. It's a an industrial zone at Zitnjak where several companies have their offices, like Chromos, Ina, and several other important companies. It was at that location that a certain amount of bomb elements landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And is that location also discussed in this report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And generally again, the same question I put to you yesterday about the other report, what kinds of damage generally speaking are discussed in this report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report also includes the large amounts of damage inflicted on properties, cars, open spaces, stores and so on and so forth. One police officer got killed as he was trying to deactivate a bomb. All in all, the damage was quite identical to the damage inflicted the previous day, but of a somewhat lesser scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you to look at a specific page now. And I believe it's page 40 or 41 in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's page 40 in the English version, and page 41 in the B/C/S. And can I see that on the e-court we'll have to go one page ahead, because actually we see a number 40 at the top of the page, please. Thank you. And if we could scroll down in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, what is discussed here on this page of the report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 41 of the official record on the inspection of the scene of incident that I prepared, there is the description of the body of a police officer who was killed while deactivating one of the bombs. According to the information I collected on the site, his injuries were sustained in the following way: In the yard of the children's hospital at Klaiceva Street he was trying to deactivate the bomb whilst he was in a squatting position, but as he was doing the deactivation process the bomb exploded and he received injuries to his head, to his torso, which resulted in his instantaneous death. He was admitted into the emergency ward of the children's hospital, but he passed away soon thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What was this police officer's name?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that he was a police officer because he wore the official police uniform. I also knew him personally because I had had numerous contacts with him previously. In addition to that, my colleague Ivan Markulin was taking part in the investigation process. On the 2nd of May, I met him at Pleso where he was doing his job.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And just -- your answer was a little long. So that I'm clear: This officer who was killed, his name was Ivan Markulin; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivan Markulin, yes. I apologise for giving you very long answers. I will try to be concise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: It's quite all right. No need to apologise. Could you please look at page 52 of your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is at page 50 in the English. And if we could scroll down in the e-court, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, what is discussed beginning on this page and then following on to subsequent pages?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As was the case with the previous report on the on-site investigation, on these pages I described the injured persons, and I was trying to include in the report, in the briefest possible terms, the name of the hospital where the injured person was received, was admitted to, a description of the injuries the person sustained, the name of the physician examining the person, and lastly to cite the medical qualification of the injuries provided by the examining physician. In this document, I'm positive that I obtained medical reports for each and every person mentioned in the report, and everything that I wrote down in the official record of the inspection of the scene of incident can be compared with the medical reports which contain the descriptions of injuries written by physicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And let me ask you to look at a particular entry. If you could go to page 56 of the report, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's on page 53 in English. If we could look about halfway down the page on e-court, please. That's fine right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, what does this report say about Luka Skracic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this report I described injuries and all the other issues I just mentioned in the same way also for Luka Skracic. However, here you can see that Dr. Romcevic qualified this injury as a serious bodily injury, but I believe it was several days later that we received the information that Luka Skracic had succumbed to his injuries. In other words, he died as a result of the injuries sustained on the 3rd of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come back to that in just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honour, I'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The exhibit number will be 802.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, we can put this report to the side for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And I would ask that another document be called up on e-court, please. The 65 ter number is 1793. I'm sorry, you have to use 1792, I apologise. There were two copies of this one, and 1792 is the one to use. Actually, if on e-court we could see the whole page there again, I think it would be easier. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, can you tell us what this document is? Are you able to see that sufficiently?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The print is somewhat small, but I hope I'll get my bearings. As far as I can see --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Actually, let me interrupt you. I don't want to strain you. If we could blow it up again and look at the bottom of the document, I guess that would be easiest. Thank you very much. Mr. Lazarevic, just focusing on the bottom part of document there, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that this has to do with the autopsy of the dead body of Luka Skracic, who sustained injuries on the 3rd of May, 1995 during the rocket attack on Zagreb, and he died in the hospital on the 6th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could turn to the next page, please, in the B/C/S. It's all on one page, Your Honours, in English. Thank you. And if we could scroll down to the bottom. There, that's fine. It's not necessary to read it out, Mr. Lazarevic, but does this confirm that you just told us and give a little bit more detail about the wounds from which he died, Luka Skracic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This autopsy report shows that Professor Skavic had come to the conclusion that Luka Skracic had died a violent death as a result of a pneumonia which had developed after having suffered explosive wounds. And the physician has found that there is a cause-effect relation between the death and the injuries that this person sustained on the 3rd of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The exhibit number is 803.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, now I'm going to hand you a binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And Your Honours, here again our experience during proofing was that the e-court was not going to be very effective for this, so what I have done is I have put some documents, mostly photographs into a binder for the witness. What I have is index, indexes, I guess, there's just one index for that binder. I have provided one to Defence counsel, and I would propose to hand them up so Your Honours can follow along with the tabs and so that everything is clear. We will also bring them up on e-court. And when we need to look at particular pages, then those will be shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I first ask about the last document we are still having on the screen, if this is the same, which I have. It's a report of -- by Professor Josip Skavic to the county court in Zagreb, investigating judge Radovan Ortinsky; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: This does not deal with the dead body of Ivan Brodar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, it deals with both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The second.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yeah, further down on the page -- it starts off with Ivan Brodar, and I believe further down the page it deals with Luka Skracic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: So it deals with two. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, now you have in front of you a binder full of documents. I would like you to look first at tab 1, the document behind tab 1. This is 65 ter number 1683. So if we could also see it on the e-court, that would be helpful, please. Mr. Lazarevic, what is contained in this document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a photographic map produced by forensic technicians of the Zagreb police administration concerning the rocket attack against the city of Zagreb. I apologise. The people who took part in conducting the on-site investigation together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And when were these maps prepared?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they were prepared immediately after the on-site investigation was completed. As soon as my colleagues returned to the office, they started preparing this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: In fact, if you turn to the second page, I think, it's 0031-2426 stamped at the -- I don't see that you have that. It's fine. Your answer is sufficiently clear. If you could then turn to plan 1, or map 1. This is 0031-2428 in e-court. It's just two pages further in the same document. There we go. Mr. Lazarevic, what is depicted on this map?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the layout of the town of Zagreb used by the crime technicians to mark the locations hit by the bombs and to mark the locations where people were killed, as well as to indicate where the damage to property was caused. We discussed that a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And if you could look just to your right, is this the same map that you see on the -- a little bit larger to your right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the same map except this one is somewhat bigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is map 17 from the map booklet, which is Exhibit 22. So we have it in a couple of different forms. And we will see which is easiest. I'm going to ask him to locate a few places so we will see which one works the best.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, which of the numbered locations that you see on the map here, which were hit on the 2nd of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 2nd of May, the following locations were hit: Mazuranica Square, Trg Marsala Tita square, the neighbourhood of Cehi in Novi Zagreb, a bit further down to the south of Botinac, as well as the neighbourhood of Zitnjak which is towards the east --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you for a second. Maybe I wasn't clear. I didn't say the second day of the shelling, but 2 May, 1995, that was my question. Which locations were hit on that day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. The first day, that is on the 2nd of May, the following locations were hit: The centre of town was hit, including Strossmayerov Square, Matica Hrvatska Street, Petrinjska Street, Boskoviceva Street, and Mrazoviceva Street That was the down-town of Zagreb. Then Draskoviceva Street was hit, as well as the intersection of Vlaska and Boskoviceva, and the front yard, as well as the building of the seventh high school in Krizaniceva Street, as well as the neighbourhood of Pleso, which is the suburbs of Velika Gorica. That was the 2nd of May, if I understood your question well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Let me focus your attention on this map. Sorry, we don't need to go forward. If we could look at the map again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And we repeat that for the transcript, for the exact names of these squares and streets, the first day, that is on the 2nd of May, you said, Witness, the following locations were hit, the centre of the town was hit, including Strossmayerov Street or square, you said, and this was also not quite clear in the transcript yesterday, so we might clarify that now at this point. And you can maybe speak a little slower when mentioning these streets or square names. If you would like to repeat that, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat. On the 2nd of May, 1995, the following locations were hit: Josip Jurij Strossmayer Square, Matica Hrvatska Street, Petrinjska Street, Boskovica Street, and Mrazoviceva Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could make one comment about how the transcript is prepared. Because these are unusual names and the key strokes sometimes don't get the spelling right, but there is someone reviewing the transcript and these names can be added in later. In fact, the court reporters have access to this report and so they can take the spellings from that. So I think the fact that it came up again without the full spellings is not lost for the record. It is just something that will have to wait until I guess at the end of the day today when it's reviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Okay. I see in yesterday's transcript this Strossmayerov Square, for example, has been corrected. Meanwhile I appreciate that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I appreciate the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I just want you to focus on the map right now, because it has some numbers on it. Can you see, if you turn the next page in your binder there, to the actual map itself rather than the legend, which numbers on the map show locations that were impacted on the 2nd of May, 1995? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On my map I see no numbers because it's far too small. Perhaps it's better if I indicate that on the large map, with your leave. Perhaps I can see the numbers clearly there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That would be fine. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number 1 marks the spot of the intersection, this is it. The intersection of Draskoviceva and Vlaska streets. At that location a streetcar was hit, or a tram, and Ms. Ana Mutevelic was killed on the spot. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Please do. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number 2 marks the spot I mentioned a minute ago. It is Josip Jurij Strossmayer Square, as well as Matica Hrvatska Street, Petrinjska Street, Boskoviceva Street and Mrazoviceva Street. That's number 2. The number 3 marks the spot where the seventh grammar school is located. The bombs fell in the courtyard, and several students were injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry to interrupt for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, one easy way to see this is if you press the video button for your screen. As the witness is referring to numbers, sometimes the video will focus right in and so it's easier to see which numbers he is pointing to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Black. We're managing reasonably well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It was something I just discovered so I thought I'd share the development.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I'm sorry for the interruption. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I have to explain the number 4. The location shown there is where the children's Klaiceva Street hospital is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Let me ask you this way. You can continue going through in order, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and for each location that you mention, please tell us on which day it was hit so that we're clear. For each location, I want to know which day, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The initial three locations, the events there happened on the 2nd of May. The location marked with the number 4, that took place on the 3rd of May. To continue, the next location is marked with the number 5. This is where Mazuranica Square is located. The fine arts academy is there as well as the Croatian National Theatre. Several people were injured, and that took place on the 3rd of May on Mazuranica Square, as well as Marsala Tita Square. Then the next location is marked with the number 6. Indicating the area of Velika Gorica; to be more precise, the neighbourhood of Pleso, where the airport is located as well. The number 6 location, the events there took place on the 2nd of May of 1995. The location marked with the number 7 is the business area of Zitnjak, and the incident took place on the 3rd of May. The last location is marked with the number 8, indicating the area in Novi Zagreb called Cehi, the neighbourhood of Cehi. As far as I know, that piece of ordnance remained unexploded. It hit the ground without any consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. This also took place on the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Are the markings on this map, are they consistent with your reports and your investigations into the events of the 2nd and 3rd of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything shown on the map, everything that was marked with numbers corresponds to the two reports we've discussed. Except that one of the reports is dated the 2nd and the other one the 3rd of May. Therefore, each date had its own document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to ask you to look for a couple of more places on the map, and to do this -- I want to try and do this on the computer. If we could zoom in on the top one-third of this map that we see on our -- or the top quarter, top left quarter, I guess. Yes, there. Let's zoom in on that portion. And perhaps a little bit more on the area where the impacts 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 are. If we could just zoom in a little bit more on that. Thank you. That's fine. If you could just centre those on the screen, I think. There. Mr. Lazarevic, I didn't intend this to be a test of your eyesight, so if you have difficulty with this, please just let me know and we can try it on the bigger map. But for instance, are you able to find Ban Jelacic Square on the computer screen? If you can't, please say so. I understand that it's not particularly clear.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I will be able to locate it, but I have no indicator.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Actually, the court usher will hand you an electronic pen so that you can actually make a mark right on to the screen. So if you can, if you could just give us the approximate location of Ban Jelacic Square, please. And if you can find it, put a letter A next -- right on top of it.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I can locate it quite precisely on the map. This long street should be Ilica Street, and Ban Jelacic Square should be a bit below my marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Could you put a letter B on Ilica Street, the street you just referred to? And maybe just trace along that street so we know which one you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is Ilica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put the letter B just next to that line at any point?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. I did so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. I can't quite see it on my screen. Perhaps it's just -- that's fine.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is on the very edge of the screen, but perhaps I can move it to the right. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Excellent, I can see that now. Thank you very much. One other question about Ban Jelacic Square. What is there at Ban Jelacic Square, what do you see when you go there? Does it have a famous statue there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On Ban Josip Jelacic Square, there is a statue there representing Ban Josip Jelacic himself. It is not in the very centre of the square, but if we draw a line splitting the square and the northern and the southern part, it is in the northern portion. If we divide it like that, it would be a few metres towards the north. But in any case, the statue itself is in the square.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And is Josip Jelacic, is he standing, or is he sitting on a horse? What does he look like; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a tall base. I can't be precise as to its height. It is made of stone. In my estimate it could be some three metres tall. On the base there is an -- an equestrian statue; there is a horse and Ban Josip Jelacic is on its back. In my estimate the height of the statue in its entirety is some five to six metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The horse and the rider correspond to the actual size of a horse and a human being.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks for your patience with those questions about that location. Do you know the address of the Croatian Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The address of the Ministry of Defence is Petar Kralj Kresimira the Fourth Square.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you think you would be able to identify that location on the map on your screen?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If you can -- if you can find it, just please put a letter C on top of it.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite difficult to get my bearings on this map, so I will try to mark it as closely and as precisely as I can. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. I know that it's not the best map. Maybe how would you describe in words the location of the Ministry of Defence in relation to some other landmark?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is easier for me to describe it in words than to point it on the map. The Ministry of Defence is located in the vicinity of the bus central station in Zagreb. A bit to the north from the station. It is also located close to the museum of people's revolution. It is down-town Zagreb. It covers the area of approximately three to -- by 400 metres. And not only the Ministry of Defence is located there, but also several other military facilities or institutions, I would call them. Perhaps someone from the armed forces would do a much better job in explaining that, but I will try to share with you what I know with a degree of certainty. There is the military hotel there adjacent to the Ministry of Defence. I believe the hotel's name is Zvonimir. Then the former -- the former JNA military club. Then there is another military building there, I don't know its function. But the entire compound, the entire area is some three by 400 metres, including various military facilities and institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thanks. We're about to take our normal break, but if you can, can you find the Banski Dvori on here; it's where the seat of government is. If you can, just put a letter D approximately on top of that location. If you can't, please just say so, and I understand.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. The letter D marks the spot, approximately. To try and simplify the matter, I wanted to say that the Banski Dvori building is to the north-west of Ban Josip Jelacic Square by some 1.000 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before the break, the reason I was hurrying is I think we need to save the screen shot to make it an exhibit. So if we could make this view of this map as marked by the witness an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Will the map, as marked by the witness please be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The exhibit number will be 804.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And this is now a convenient time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, you will be relieved to know I'm not going to ask you to draw anymore. I do have just a couple more questions about places in Zagreb in general. Are you aware of any military barracks in Zagreb or near Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to mention several barracks that were active at the time. But I am afraid I might not mention and cover all of them because I'm not a military man myself, and I have never had any dealings with the military. At the time there was the barracks at Sarajevska Street in Zagreb, which was operational, which was formally called Marshal Tito barracks. There was another barracks at Velika Gorica at the Pleso airport where the JNA had also been stationed. There was another barracks at Borogaj, the name of which I can't recall at present, but it used to be called Dusan Corkovic barracks. At Maksimirska Street there was one barracks located between Kvaternik Square and the Dinamo stadium. Furthermore, there was the barracks at Crnomerec. These are the barracks I can think of. There may have been others I forgot. There was one barracks at Samobor and another one at Jastrebarsko, but all of these barracks are further away from Zagreb, some 15 to 20 kilometres, perhaps even more. I'd like to say that I can't give you a full answer. I can only respond to the extent I remember. The knowledge of military facilities was not directly related to the duties I had to perform for the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I understand that. Thank you very much. Let me ask you to turn to plan 2 in that same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're still in 65 ter number 1683. And if we could turn to plan 2, please. It should just be two pages further in -- on the e-court, I think. Yes, and if we could see the next page. Could we see the next page, the actual map itself as opposed to the legend? Thank you. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, what do we see here on the screen now? What is this image?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Plan 2 consists of a diagram drawn by the crime technician who took part in the on-site investigation. In short, marked with number 1 is the location at which the dead body of Ana Mutevelic was found. She was found lying on the sidewalk. What is also depicted here are two tram carriages that pulled to a stop and which could be found on the scene at the time of the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What about number 2. What does number 2 there signify?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2 depicts the position or the site at Vlaska Street which is colloquially called Stara Vlaska Street. In addition to his vehicle, the body of Damir Dracic was found there. He was also found lying on the sidewalk. According to the information we obtained, the injuries -- or, rather, the person sustained his injuries at the time when he was inside the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And what about number 3, please?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3 marks the site where Stjepan Krhanj was found during the on-site investigation. He was found in the courtyard of Vlaska Street at number 41 before the gate booth of Export-drvo company. The persons I just mentioned were the persons whose bodies had not been removed from the scene of the incident, and their bodies were there at the point when ambulances arrived, which led us to the conclusion that they -- their death had been instantaneous, which explains why they hadn't been transported anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: At the top of the map, or towards the top of the map you see a small red symbol that looks kind of like a tiny explosion. Could you tell us what that signifies?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On that spot in the courtyard of Sostariceva Street, a crater was found in the ground which still held the debris originating from the surface-to-surface rocket, also known as Orkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: In this view we can also see that there are quite a number of small red dots around the map. What do those signify?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The red dots depict the numerous sites on either asphalt or soil surfaces where bombs landed and where the blast took place. At all these sites we found the sort of damage that is typical of the effect the bomb involved normally has. Of course this doesn't even remotely show all the sites. There were many, many more such sites than are, in fact, depicted here with the red dots.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And I won't go through all the maps in this document one by one, but could you just look through the document, and do plans 3, 4, 5, 6 all the way up until 10, do they show other locations where rockets and bomblets impacted? You can just -- you know, this document is also in your binder, so in addition to the screen, you can actually look at the documents in the binder.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: We don't need to go through each one. If you could just tell me if they all refer to various locations where a rocket or bomblets impacted. I just don't think it's necessary to spend the time in court; that's the only reason.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is precisely one of the sites that I mentioned a moment ago. That's the site of impact at Strossmayer Square and Sostariceva Street. That's the diagram showing the sites of impact of the bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. And listen carefully to my question: Do the other plans that come after that in the document, do they -- does each plan show another location? Without us going through each map, does each one show a location relevant to the things we've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. Each map shows the locations I have been mentioning before, and which had to -- do with the 2nd and the 3rd of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be admitted into evidence, please, and receive a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The exhibit number will be 805.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lazarevic, I'm going to continue my way through the binder, and I'm going to show you a series of documents that consist mostly of photographs. I'd like you -- I'd like to start with the document behind tab 2, which is trial Exhibit 386.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If it's easier to find according to the 65 ter number, it's 1644, is the 65 ter number. Thank you. If we could go to the second page on e-court maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. This is the document produced by crime technicians, and which concerns the rocket attack against Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And have you, before you came to The Hague, had you seen many or all of the photos in this document and the other ones in the binder, had you seen those before?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photographs that we have before us are familiar. I can't say that I saw each and every one of them, but I saw them back at my office before this photo file was put together, and they were therefore familiar to me. As I said, the photo file wasn't compiled by myself but by my colleagues from another department, the crime technicians department. But we did the job together in that they consulted me. Therefore, I can say that I am familiar with the photographs, that I saw them before coming here to The Hague, and I had occasion to see them on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. What locations are covered in this particular document, this particular set of photographs?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular set of photographs, as the cover page itself says, covered the location of Draskoviceva and Vlaska Streets, which we mentioned before in the context of those markings numbers 1, 2 and 3, where the bodies of Ms. Ana Mutevelic, Mr. Damir Dacic and Mr. Stjepan Krhanj were found. Specifically on photograph number 1 we see the entire length of the street or, rather, almost the entire length of Draskoviceva Street. The photograph was taken from the direction of the central railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. I'm not going to ask you to look at each photograph, but I will just take you in a moment to a couple specific ones. But one more general question: What kinds of damage are shown in the photographs in this document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document shows the damage typically produced in the explosion of explosive devices, especially after the explosion of KB-1 bombs, or bomblets, and the damage incurred was that to the property, meaning buildings, cars, open spaces, pavements, and lastly and unfortunately inflicted on persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to ask you to look at a few specific photos. And as I do this, from some of the photos, I think you could recognise the people at issue, and so I would ask the video booth if they could just not show these on the public broadcast. We will see it on e-court, but I just think out of courtesy it's better if it doesn't get publicly broadcast. Mr. Lazarevic, please turn to photos F-35 and F-36. These can be found on page 0031-2327.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What do we see in these two photographs?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photograph number 35 shows the body of Ana Mutevelic, who was killed. This is an aerial view photo, whereas on photograph number 36 we have the same photograph, but it's a closer shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. The next --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same body, that is to say, of the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. The next few photos, and we don't even need to see these on e-court. Some of them are quite graphic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just interrupt?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There's something next to the body, on the right side of the body, I don't know if it looks like a smaller human being or whether it's a parcel. Is the witness able to tell us what that is? Also lying next to the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Which photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could zoom in on F-36, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I don't know if you are -- are you able to tell --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you see what I'm talking about? Just to the right of the body there is something that looks like a smaller human being there. But I don't know what it is. On the pavement, lying next to the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If you see that, Mr. Lazarevic. Do you know what that is, could you tell His Honour what that is?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try answer the question. I took the liberty of flipping a few pages ahead, and I arrived to photograph number 40, where one can get a somewhat better view of the same site. And as far as I can see, that is definitely not a dead body of some other person. I suppose this to be -- how shall I put it, a piece of clothing, a cloth that was used to cover the body before the arrival of the police, and the police removed the piece of clothing in order to be able to take the photograph. I suppose it was the ambulance staff, or perhaps some of the residents who brought out a piece of cloth or a sheet to cover the body. At any rate, on photographs 41 and 42 one can ascertain that this was the case, that this was indeed something that was used to cover the body until the police arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We don't to look at them on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: But, Mr. Lazarevic, in fact, do the next few photographs up to F-44 show more details of the injuries to Mrs. Mutevelic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think photograph 41 offers the best view of an explosive wound to the bones of the head, just behind the ear, which I believe could have led to the death of the person, because we have the artery there which takes the blood to the brain. This of course is forensic piece of information that I can furnish. I cannot go into any medical details.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I understand that. Thank you. If we could turn to page 0031-2336 to photos F-53 and F-54. And again, Mr. Lazarevic, whose -- what do we see here in these two photographs?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two photographs show one section of the old Vlaska Street, Stara Vlaska, with a car parked on the sidewalk, and next to the car there is the dead body of Damir Dracic on the pavement. The body was also covered over. Probably the situation is the same as before, someone must have taken out a blanket, it seems, before the arrival of the police, and covered the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could turn to the next page, please. What do we see there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we are seeing here is the mechanical damage to the front windshield at the side of the driver of the car here. The explosion impact, or rather the -- there was an explosion here, and the impact pierced the windshield.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, we don't need to see these particular photos, but do the next -- do the photos on the following pages up to F-63 show more views of Mr. Dracic's injuries?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see F-63 on the screen, and the document doesn't show clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I don't want to -- don't need to show them on the screen, but just, do the next few photos on the next few pages show details of his injuries?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I remember, from my examining the site, there were very many explosive wounds all over his body. There were several wounds to his head, his body and the extremities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could move to page 0031-2353, and just look briefly at photos F-88 and F-89. I wonder if we could see those on the e-court, please. What do we see in these two photos, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it on the screen now as well. We can see mechanical damage inflicted on the car by the bomb explosion, precisely on the edge between the windshield and the roof of the car. The damage is consistent in the fact that the roof was pierced through, and around the hole we have these small indentations, which are typical of the effect the pieces of shrapnel would have during the impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And could we look now at photographs F-98 and F-99, which can be found on page 0031-2358, if we could see those on e-court, please. Although again I would ask that these continue not to be publicly broadcast. Mr. Lazarevic, what do we see on these two photographs?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two photographs show the dead body of Stjepan Krhanj, who was found in the yard of Vlaska Street at number 41. As I said, he was next to the doorman's booth of the Export-drvo company. As the photograph shows, he had the least number of injuries, but unfortunately he succumbed to his wound. We have the wound to his chest and to his right leg. All these injuries were inflicted on the 2nd of May. At the sites Draskoviceva and Vlaska Streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need to pull up the following photographs at all. But are the rest -- well, actually, if you could go to photograph F-137 in your booklet there. And if you just look, from there to the rest of the document, are those essentially detailed photos of the injuries suffered by the three people that you have mentioned, Damir Dacic, Stjepan Krhanj, and Ana Mutevelic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't have them on my screen, but I have managed to locate them here. So far as I can recognise, the photographs were taken in the Institute for Forensic Medicine and Criminology at Salata number 11 in Zagreb, where we can also see dead bodies with numerous injuries all over the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess this is an album?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I would -- my plan was to go one by one through the documents in the binder, so it's -- I don't know if -- if you call it an album, but this particular document is -- I think -- the case manager helpfully tells me it's already in evidence, Your Honour. It's trial Exhibit 386, I had forgotten that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: We can go to the next document, which is not yet in evidence. It's 65 ter number 1646.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And Mr. Lazarevic, it will be behind tab 3 in your binder. I don't have any questions about specific photographs in this one, Mr. Lazarevic, but could you just tell us very briefly which location is at issue in this document.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the location of Matica Hrvatska Street. On that street there are only two buildings, one of which being the police administration for the city of Zagreb. On that police building we can see some damage to the roof and to the upper floors because those parts of the building were also hit by the bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that's sufficient. We don't need to go into more detail for now on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could it be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are sure it is not already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: 99 per cent sure, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And once again, is it an album? Do you admit the entire album, or do you admit just one photo? And I have only seen the cover of it. It has never been paged through on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason I'm doing it this way is because each album or document is what I would call it, to avoid confusion with the binder, which contains several of them, but each tab on the index here contains a number of photographs. Many of them are repetitive of the same kind of damage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you want the whole tab.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The whole tab, exactly, that would be my preference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine. What 65 ter is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: This one is 65 ter number 1646.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the documents constituting 65 ter 1646 please be given an exhibit number. They are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. They will be 806.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can we please see on the e-court, 65 ter number 1648.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And Mr. Lazarevic, this will be behind tab 4 in your binder. And perhaps if we go to the second page in e-court. Mr. Lazarevic, there you have it. What's contained in this document, in this set of photographs? What location is at issue?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the location of Petrinjska Street. That is a part of Petrinjska Street concerning the attack that occurred on the 2nd of May. It is adjacent or immediately next to the police administration building, about 10 to 15 metres further up the street. That's the second police building at number 30. On several floors of the building there were various police departments, such as the administration, the referencing unit and so on and so forth. In any case, the entire building was used by the police. To try to help you to picture it, it is adjacent to the central police station, but that other building looks on another street. Therefore, addresses are different, although they are semi-detached.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to ask you to look at a particular page. It's 0031-2142. And if you could please look at photograph F-33. What do we see in photograph F-33, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the F-33 photograph we see a mechanical-type damage on the tarmac, which was hit by the bomb, and impacted. Therefore, there is some damage to the tarmac, there is a crater, and around the crater there are numerous small indentations caused by fragments or shrapnel. We also see pieces of tile; that's in red colour. That was still before the debris was taken away. The police took these photographs concerning the situation as they found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. We have still quite a bit of ground to cover, so if you could try to be fairly succinct in your answers, please, we will go a little more quickly. Please look at photographs -- well, beginning at page 0031-2149, and I'm interested in photographs F-47 really all the way up to F-68. If you could look in your binder and maybe on the screen it will help you. Does the photo F-47 on the screen and the following photographs, do they show damage to the roof of this building at issue here?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is damage to the roof of the two police buildings. The building of the central police station at Strossmayer Square number 3, and the adjacent building at Petrinjska Street, number 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And maybe we can just flip through them fair quickly, the next several pages on the e-court, please. It's not necessary to blow up each particular photograph. Each page of two photographs will be fine. Thank you. And the next page. And the next page. Thank you. I think that's illustrative. Mr. Lazarevic, did any of the Orkan bomblets or rockets knock down any buildings in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, not a single building was knocked down. And the damage that occurred on the buildings did not call for any demolishing. There were no such -- there was no such damage to the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What kind of damage did they generally cause to buildings?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The damage caused by the explosion of the bombs was to the extent as we have already seen it. For example, on the roofs we had broken tiles, and in this case we can see that the thermal insulation was damaged. Window-panes burst, and the facades were damaged. But other than that, there was no extensive damage. On occasion a wall or a ceiling would incur a crack, but other than that, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, yesterday we saw a clip showing a building -- or cars on fire outside a building. I think that's where the body of Ms. Mutevelic was found; I'm not quite sure now. And fire brigade people were there, trying to douse the fire. Were there no such fires elsewhere that weren't uncontrollable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The fire we could see on the recording yesterday was at Strossmayer Square, in front of the central police station there. In that location there were no killed. You mentioned the dead body of Mrs. Ana Mutevelic. On that location ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the location of where we could see the body of Mrs. Ana Mutevelic, there was no fire. As far as I remember, there was a minor fire on a passenger vehicle, a car owned by Mr. Damir Dracic, whereby he was killed himself. I believe it was under the hood of the engine. It was put out fairly quickly, and on the photographs we can see the traces of suit and of the fire extinguishing substance that was used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess the nub of my question, forget about the body of the dead person there. The nub of my question: Were there no other fires that -- that are similar to the one that we saw and that weren't uncontrollable in burnt places. That's all I wanted to know. If you could just answer verbally rather than shake your head, then we can get it on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were no fires in other locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. At this point could I ask that 65 ter number 1648, which is on our screen, be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 65 ter number 1648 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The exhibit number will be 807.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we please now see 65 ter number 1650.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And Mr. Lazarevic, this will be behind tab 5 in your binder. If we could go to the second page on the e-court, please. Mr. Lazarevic, what location is covered by these photos now that we're looking at? In this document, I mean to say.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the location of Strossmayer Square, numbers 1 to 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And is this the same area that we saw in the video earlier in your testimony, that His Honour Judge Moloto just referred to?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. I would ask you to look at one specific page. It's photographs F-87 and 88, and the page is 0031-2210. If we could see those on the e-court, please. Thank you. If we could just zoom out so we see both photographs is fine. What do we see in these photographs, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On photographs numbers 87 and 88 we can see the mechanical-type damage caused by bomb explosion on the roof of the central police station, or as it is now called, the first police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document, which is 65 ter number 1650, could that be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document number 65 ter 1650 is admitted into evidence. May it please be begin an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The exhibit number is 808.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The next document is trial Exhibit 385. It's already in evidence. And Mr. Lazarevic, it will be behind tab 6 in the binder. If you could turn to that, please. And just briefly, which location is at issue here in these -- in this document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the location of Krizaniceva Street, where the seventh Zagreb grammar school is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And if on the e-court we could turn to page 0031-2230, we should see photographs F-5 and F-6. And perhaps if we can zoom in on photograph F-5, please. I'm not sure how easy it is to see there. But Mr. Lazarevic, in this photograph and then in the photograph below, which is F-6, can we please scroll down to that, are these more -- or are these examples of damage to the walls of a building? Is that what we see there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see the playground for students, and that is the photograph number 5. On the photograph number 6, we can see the building itself. On its facade there are several impacts caused by the mechanical force of the explosion of the bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you could look four pages further to photographs F-13 and F-14, which are on page 0031-2234. Can you identify what's shown in these photographs? You see them on the screen now, or if it's easier to find them in your binder.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On photographs F-13 and F-14 we see fragments of an Orkan rocket. We have here parts of the tin casing or the so-called container, within which bombs or bomblets are located.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Those are all my questions for that document, which is already in evidence. So we can move to the next tab, tab 7 in your binder. This will be 65 ter Exhibit 1653. If we could see that on the e-court, please. Mr. Lazarevic, which location is discussed -- or is depicted in this document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the location of the place or neighbourhood, being the suburbs of Velika Gorica. In particular, Plepeliceva and Kusceviceva Streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could look at page 0031-2587, photographs 3 and 4 there. Mr. Lazarevic, what do we see in these two photos?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On these two photographs -- I guess I don't have the right ones. On the screen we can see some fragments of the surface-to-surface rocket used with the Orkan system.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. At page 0031-2603 should be photographs F-45 and F-46. If you could try to find those, please. And just to double-check, we're behind tab 7 right now in your binder, Mr. Lazarevic. Yeah. What do we see in photographs F-45 and F-46, if you can make it out?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can make out what's on the photographs. It's a roofing. Somewhat to the left of the chimney, there is damage to the tiles. Tiles -- some tiles were shattered due to an impact of a bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we turn to the next page on e-court, please? On the bottom photograph, Mr. Lazarevic, F-48, can you tell what it is that's shown there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not particularly clear, but as far as I can see I presume this is the place where the roof was damaged and pierced by a projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And just a couple more photographs on this document. At 0031-2613, photographs F-65 and F-66. Could you please tell us what's shown in these two photographs?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On these two photographs we have crates, a pyrotechnist's collected unexploded ordnance belonging to the KB-1 system.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could this be admitted into evidence, this is 65 ter 1653.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 65 ter 1653 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The exhibit number will be 809.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next document is 65 ter Exhibit 1654.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And Mr. Lazarevic, this will be behind tab 8 now in your binder. I won't spend much time on this, but just very briefly could you tell me what location is addressed in this document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this document we see the location of the airport of Pleso. Within its perimeter we've located a place where -- we've detected a place where a cluster bomb impacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And how far is this from the airport itself? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the civilian airport, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is within its perimeter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be admitted into evidence, please. It's 65 ter number 1654.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 65 ter number 1654 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the exhibit number is 810.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: A few more documents, Mr. Lazarevic. The next one behind tab 9 in your binder is trial Exhibit 387, which is already in evidence. Mr. Lazarevic, what location or locations are addressed in this document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see, several locations were addressed here. The first of them being the site at Klaiceva number 16, where the children's hospital is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And do photographs F-1 to F-24, do those show damage to the children's hospital on Klaiceva Street?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Peripherally the premises of the waiting-room and the gynaecological office were impacted. The damage was inflicted in terms of the window-panes having been shattered, and the -- and cracks made in the facade. It's actually in the vicinity of this wall with the cracks in and the window shattered, that the pyrotechnist was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Let me show you F-26 which is 0031-2478.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that a 2478?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: It should be, Your Honour. I didn't bring a hard copy. If we could -- does it not go to 2478.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not on my screen. My screen is 2477.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On my screen 2477 is the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, are you able to find photograph F-26 there in your binder?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps this is an e-court problem that I not discovered. Maybe we could have the photo shown on the ELMO for that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, very well, but I don't think it's an e-court problem because my screen says 12 out of 12, page 12 out of 12, and that's 2477.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document is, in fact, longer than that. The e-court problem I meant was we apparently didn't upload the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Human problem, nothing wrong with the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While we're doing that, can I ask the witness a question. Mr. Lazarevic, you said that part of the damage to the Klaiceva children's hospital was cracks to the building, to the walls. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not the walls themselves, perhaps the outside part of the wall, the facade itself, but there were no cracks. There were pock-marks. The window-panes were shattered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I probably misheard you. Okay. Never mind. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we see on my -- having pushed the ELMO button on my computer I'm seeing photograph F-25. Could we see photograph F-26, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, what happened at the place pictured in photo F-26?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the site where the bomblet exploded in the hands of pyrotechnist Ivan Markulin. There is damage to the concrete floor there, and this place has been marked with number 1. The pyrotechnist was still showing signs of life at the time the paramedics arrived, he was transferred to the emergency ward of the hospital where he died later on, and this is what we see on the photograph here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, seeing as the rest of the photographs, we didn't get them into e-court. I'll just move it -- actually, this document is already in evidence, so I will move on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we see 65 ter number 1658 on the e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And Mr. Lazarevic, this will be behind tab 10 in your binder. That's right. It's 65 ter number 1658. Mr. Lazarevic, just briefly, what location is dealt with in this document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the location at Zitnjak, the industrial zone at Zitnjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like you to look at two photographs. They're on page 0031-2456 and they're photographs F-9 and F-10. And perhaps we can zoom in on the bottom photograph, F-10, please. And, Mr. Lazarevic, can you tell us what we see here in photograph F--10?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows parts of the tin cladding of the rocket casing, and I mean the Orkan surface-to-surface system.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, may 65 ter number 1658 be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 65 ter number 1658 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the exhibit number will be 811.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: One more document to look at and it's Trial Exhibit 775. Mr. Lazarevic, this will be the final document there in your binder. Please have a -- have a look at this document, in fact flip through the whole thing and tell us what's contained in this document, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I'm not sure what I'm supposed to look at. I still have the old photograph on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes. It just takes a second. They'll bring it up. There it is. But I'd like you to -- to take a moment and look at each page of this document. Don't just focus on the first page. Take a moment, look through every page of the document, and tell us what's included there. It's probably not necessary to read all the text, I just want you to look through the photographs that come later in the document, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to give you an answer, and if you find it inadequate, then please put follow-up questions to me. In this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Have you looked at all the pages of the document? Just flip through them. We have time. Take a moment. Are there more pages than just that first two pages?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
